# `css/no-invalid-position-declaration`

**Declarations sit inside rules**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-css` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-css` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | CSS, SCSS |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (the selector it was meant for is the author's call) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.1.0 |
| **Ported from** | `stylelint/no-invalid-position-declaration` |

## What it checks

A declaration sits inside a style rule, in an at-rule nested inside one, or in an at-rule that takes descriptors — never at the top level or directly inside a top-level `@media`.

**Why:** A declaration with no rule around it applies to nothing; the browser drops it.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-css
pip install codelaw-rules-css
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:css/recommended` sets it to `error`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:css/recommended"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"css/no-invalid-position-declaration" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — a scope of your own needs `files`:

```toml
[scope.legacy]
files = ["src/legacy/**/*.css"]
rules = { "css/no-invalid-position-declaration" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"css/no-invalid-position-declaration" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"css/no-invalid-position-declaration" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"css/no-invalid-position-declaration" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "css/no-invalid-position-declaration": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **CSS:** `/* codelaw-ignore css/no-invalid-position-declaration: <reason> */`
- **SCSS:** `// codelaw-ignore css/no-invalid-position-declaration: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `/* codelaw-ignore css/no-invalid-position-declaration expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason> */`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule css/no-invalid-position-declaration --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain css/no-invalid-position-declaration       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule css/no-invalid-position-declaration  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>                       # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Move the declaration into the style rule it belongs to.

## Examples

### CSS

#### Don't

```css
color: red;
```

#### Do

```css
a {
  color: red;
}
```
### SCSS

#### Don't

```scss
color: red;
```

#### Do

```scss
a {
  color: red;
}
```
